newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open steady then plunge further.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open steady then plunge further.

text.p: Singapore shares opened almost unchanged on Tuesday in very low volume but then resumed the downtrend seen on Monday.
"All the early top 10 volume stocks were traded in (off-market) crosses," said one dealer. "No one wants to do anything until there are clear signs of a recovery."
Top of the actives was Causeway Investment which saw a cross of one million shares at Singapore $1.45 each. Last month, the firm denied takeover rumours after a rash of similar crosses.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 15.85 lower at 2,112.95 points by 0140 GMT.

Dealers said part of the reason for the slump in local shares was Morgan Stanley's recent down-weighting of Singapore in its Asian stock indices. But they noted that Morgan Stanley's previous adjustment, which raised Singapore's weighting, had had little impact on the local market.
"Whatever influence it had is almost over now," said one.
Dealers said the market should recover once there were signs the current economic downturn in Singapore was ending.
"About the best we can hope for right now is a fourth quarter rally," said one dealer.
